en: Osmium is twice as dense as lead, boasting a massive density of 22.59 grams per cubic centimeter.
Liquid water expands by about nine percent in volume when it freezes into solid ice.
At 20 degrees Celsius, a maximum of 36 grams of table salt can dissolve in 100 milliliters of water.
Pure water boils at exactly 100 degrees Celsius at sea level, but boils at lower temperatures on high mountains.
A single tiny drop of water contains approximately 1.5 sextillion individual water molecules.
The Sun is made of superheated plasma, reaching core temperatures of about 15 million degrees Celsius.
Milk is a colloid containing about 87 percent water, with tiny liquid fat globules suspended throughout.
Mixing five grams of baking soda with vinegar produces approximately 1.3 liters of carbon dioxide gas.
Tungsten has the highest melting point of all metals, requiring 3,422 degrees Celsius to become a liquid.
When liquid water turns into steam, it expands to occupy about 1,700 times more space.
Bronze is a solid metal mixture typically containing 88 percent copper and 12 percent tin.
Because the human body is 60 percent water, a 30-kilogram child contains roughly 18 kilograms of water.
